title: Jacob's ladder (Genesis 28:10–22)
hookLine: a stone pillow, a stairway of angels: surely the Lord is in this place, and I knew it not
carry: god was here and I didn't know

cards: A young man is walking alone toward Haran, fast. Behind him, a brother who has said he means to kill him once their father dies. Ahead, an uncle he's never met, in a country he's never seen.
He has the blessing he stole, and not much else. The sun goes down in the middle of nowhere. No inn, no town.
He puts one of the stones lying around under his head and lies down on the ground. The kind of night people spend in airports, or on a friend's floor. Not a place anyone would pick to meet God.

teach.h: A STAIRWAY, ANGELS GOING BOTH WAYS.
teach.b: Then Jacob dreams. In the King James Bible: "behold a ladder set up on the earth, and the top of it reached to heaven: and behold the angels of God ascending and descending on it."
Some translations say stairway; translators aren't sure of the Hebrew. Either way, heaven and earth are joined, and the traffic runs both ways. Above it, God speaks, and does not scold the runaway.

He repeats the promise made to Abraham and Isaac, and adds something personal: I am with you, I will keep you wherever you go, I will bring you back. The text doesn't say Jacob has done anything to earn it.
He wakes up afraid and says: "Surely the LORD is in this place; and I knew it not." And: "this is none other but the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven."
He sets his stone pillow up as a pillar, pours oil on it, and renames the place. It was called Luz.
He calls it Bethel: beth, house; El, God. What made it holy? Not a temple, not a priest, not a good week.

teach.h: SURELY THE LORD IS IN THIS PLACE.
teach.b: A rock in the middle of nowhere, and a man on the run.

In John's Gospel, Jesus tells Nathanael he will see the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of man, and some Christians hear Jesus himself as the stairway. Jewish tradition has its own readings.
And some readers simply keep Jacob's surprise: God was here, and he didn't know.

how: Christians often read Jacob's dream alongside John 1:51, where Jesus speaks of angels ascending and descending upon the Son of man, and the phrase "house of God" has long been used of churches and places of prayer.

o: a city of refuge for people on the run
a temple Jacob built for his family
house of God, Jacob's name for a stony place

games.q: what's inside the dream — tap the pairs.
p: set up as a pillar, with oil

s: Bethel was the place's name before Jacob came
it was called Luz. Jacob renamed it Bethel, house of God.
in the dream, the angels go up and down
"ascending and descending on it": traffic in both directions.
God scolds Jacob for stealing the blessing
in the dream God repeats the promise and adds: I am with you, I will keep you.

games.q: you're Jacob. you wake at dawn on a stony hillside, shaking from a dream of heaven opened above you. what do you do?
o: get moving fast and try to forget it.
set up your stone pillow as a pillar and name the place.
go back home and make peace with your brother.
games.why: he stands the stone up, pours oil on it, and renames the place Bethel, house of God. going home comes much later.

practice: Wherever you are, a kitchen, a bus seat, a desk, rest your eyes on one plain thing, a cup, a step, a doorframe, and let it be your stone. Think of something that happened in a place like this that mattered more than it looked.
If you pray, say Jacob's words quietly, surely the Lord is in this place; if you don't, just let the place be more than it seems.

wordCard.voice: Bethel. House of God, in Hebrew. The name Jacob gave a stony place where he slept on the run and found he wasn't alone.

orig.note: Hebrew: beth, house, and El, God. house of God.
